svg.title: Proof. Applying q to the displayed reader cancels qi = I and recovers Km exactly. Similarly qΠZ m = Πmq, and every finite identity obtained by composing these maps follows by inserting these inverse identities at each slot. A tested residual is the difference of the original tested cluster and its finite reader expansion. Each term has the same scalar reading, so the residual and its absolute bound are identical. Infinite summations use the original convergence warrant, as in Theorem B.1. No inversion of Πm is used: its discarded tail is retained in the residual. The argument applies to each original nested cluster and spectator domain without altering its scale ratios or error exponents.
